checkpoints.description: [1/6] Plan: add a literature-based e-consent flow and a privacy-preserving email data-return path for future research articles

impact_assessment.why: The user wants Noesis to collect data for future articles; that requires documented informed consent, a pseudonymous participant code, and a user-triggered way to send the export to the study team's email without adding a server or silent data transmission
impact_assessment.benefits: Opt-in research participation; bilingual EN/TR consent; versioned consent record in the export; email draft + JSON download; no account, no server, no automatic send
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new storage keys, a new consent screen, export schema fields and Settings panel; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: existing local data remains valid, new optional fields
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first storage/UI/export tests, pure email-draft builder, no network code, browser proof of consent + download, full gates

checkpoints.description: [2/6] Impl: two e-consent context records; researchSettings/researchConsent/researchEmail storage; bilingual EN/TR consent screen; ResearchDataPanel; export research metadata; local JSON download + mailto draft with manual attach; withdrawal and contact-change re-consent; Settings and App wiring

[1/5] Plan: log every session start, completion and early ending so adherence and dropout are measurable in research exports

impact_assessment.why: The review makes adherence a primary metric (R22) and the export currently contains only completed sessions; dropout cannot be measured, which blocks the app as a data collector for future articles. A pilot RCT in computerized training reported 38.5%/57.1% dropout (PMID 30881315), so starts and early endings must be logged.
impact_assessment.benefits: Session-level adherence log with seed, timestamps, blocks completed and arm; export and Settings summary; no server and no change to cognitive scores
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new storage key, export field and Settings prop; dependency: none; concurrency: no cross-tab guarantees beyond existing local storage; state: old exports remain valid because adherence defaults to []
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first storage/export/UI tests, explicit start/complete/abort paths, dangling-start closure on a new session, full gates and browser proof

[1/5] Plan: add analysis-ready CSV exports for session blocks and adherence events, grounded in FAIR/data-reuse guidance

impact_assessment.why: The JSON export is complete but not directly analysis-ready in R/SPSS; researchers must flatten nested results and adherence events by hand, which invites transcription errors and weakens reuse. FAIR data guidance calls for interoperable, reusable formats and metadata.
impact_assessment.benefits: Stable CSV headers, one row per block/event, escaped cells, complete metrics JSON, local download; no server or PII change
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new export builders and Settings buttons; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no storage change
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first CSV/UI tests, a browser download proof, FAIR note and full gates

checkpoints.description: [2/5] Impl: sessions CSV one row per block with metrics_json/motivation_json; adherence CSV one row per event; RFC 4180 quoting; date-stamped local downloads; Settings buttons; R61 and ADR-043; DATA_EXPORT_AND_REUSE.md

[3/5] Verified: 29 Python + 325 Vitest; typecheck/build clean; ai:verify 400/400; review 116/277 valid; browser proof sessions CSV header + 1 row, adherence CSV header + 1 row, consoleErrors []; UI audit no horizontal scroll/tiny text; aikit check 6/6; checklists: passed
Task 'noesis-csv-export' completed successfully.
[1/4] Plan: add a self-describing export manifest and field-level data dictionary for reproducible research reuse

impact_assessment.why: The JSON export has a version and counts, but not the app/review/consent provenance or a field-level dictionary, so a study team cannot tell which evidence version and consent version produced a file; FAIR reuse needs metadata that travels with the data.
impact_assessment.benefits: Self-describing JSON exports, explicit app/evidence/consent provenance, count summary, and a data dictionary covering JSON and CSV fields
impact_assessment.risks: contract: additive export field and shared version constants; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: old exports remain valid
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first export tests, browser proof manifest checks, data dictionary review, full gates

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Impl: manifest with app/schema/review/dictionary/consent versions and counts; centralized appMeta; Settings footer uses review v1.1; DATA_DICTIONARY.md covers JSON/CSV; R62 and ADR-044

[1/4] Plan: surface the neutral session completion summary in the Menu History tab, not only Settings

impact_assessment.why: Adherence data is now logged and exported, but the user only sees it in Settings. The review supports self-monitoring and feedback on behaviour (R23), and a visible neutral summary makes the history meaningful without loss framing.
impact_assessment.benefits: Started/completed/ended-early counts and completion rate in Menu History; same local data as the export; no new storage
impact_assessment.risks: contract: PracticeMenuScreen prop; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first menu test, neutral copy review, browser/UI audit, full gates
